content.comment_body: Hello, A few weeks ago, I created a small program based on the following requirement: A single push button with two possible functions, which can be connected to either input I1 or I2, controlling two lighting circuits. By cycling the push button, different combinations are achieved: For I1: 00-01-10-11 (all OFF, circuit 1 ON & circuit 2 OFF, circuit 1 OFF & circuit 2 ON, both ON). For I2: 01-10-11, and a long press (>0.5 sec) resets all to OFF (00). The code I attached works well, but I'm interested in knowing if there's a simpler or more efficient way to handle this. Any advice? [user_name]
Are you suggesting something similar to this?

Please check the attachment for a straightforward approach. It differs slightly in function but integrates all four combinations. The timer module can be removed since the combinations are available within the logic. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you [user_name] and [user_name], It's great to see two solutions I hadn't considered before. I also discovered the purpose of the M8 block, which I hadn't used previously.

analysis.insight_summary: Community members shared insights on code simplification and alternative logic for managing two inputs to control two outputs, using a cycling push button in a lighting scenario. The initial solution was reliable, but users expressed interest in more streamlined logic and learning about underutilized blocks. Feedback highlighted that features allowing intuitive logic configuration, plus documentation of lesser-known modules, improved the user experience.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a more straightforward and optimized method to achieve multi-state output control via push button inputs, ideally using logic modules or blocks they may not be familiar with.
